explanation: Weekly manual reviews cover servers and availability alerts, but disclosure intake and process-weakness detection are incomplete.
customerRisk: Missed weaknesses could disrupt the public-information workspace or expose information agencies placed there.
providerCompensation: A small inventory and daily uptime checks make operational changes easier to investigate.
agencyCompensation: Agencies should retain source copies and avoid sensitive data or critical workloads.

explanation: A weekly spreadsheet review tracks major findings, but ownership and exploitation checks are not complete for every vulnerability.
customerRisk: Unassigned findings may remain open and cause preventable service interruptions.
providerCompensation: An on-call operator isolates unstable components and keeps restoration instructions current.
agencyCompensation: Agencies should keep an alternate publication channel and avoid critical workloads.

explanation: We have not yet recorded failures of our detection and response processes as vulnerabilities.
customerRisk: Repeated review failures may hide exposures that affect agency information or availability.
providerCompensation: The weekly operations meeting assigns corrective work in a separate issue list.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can request unresolved process issues before expanding their use.

explanation: Simple isolation and backups support resilience, but the small team has not redesigned shared components that complicate recovery.
customerRisk: A shared-component failure could interrupt multiple agency workspaces.
providerCompensation: We test restores monthly and restrict administrative access.
agencyCompensation: Agencies should maintain an alternate service and avoid time-critical dependencies.

explanation: Budget limits keep vulnerability detection and response largely manual, beyond basic uptime alerts.
completionTargetExplanation: We have not selected an affordable monitoring service.
customerRisk: Manual checks can miss emerging weaknesses between reviews.
providerCompensation: Operators inspect the small resource inventory weekly and investigate uptime alarms daily.
agencyCompensation: Agencies should report unusual behavior promptly and keep sensitive data elsewhere.

explanation: Changes receive manual checks because our deployment scripts do not trigger vulnerability detection.
customerRisk: A release could introduce a weakness that affects agency access or content.
providerCompensation: The operator reviews changed settings and tests rollback before release.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can defer new integrations until the release review is available.

explanation: Manual assessment uses restricted maintenance access without disabling protective controls or opening additional network paths.
Operators check major images against KEVs, but the release checklist does not yet cover every machine component.
customerRisk: An overlooked component could expose agency workspaces to known exploitation.
providerCompensation: We limit exposed services and remove unused components.
agencyCompensation: Agencies should avoid sensitive content and restrict unnecessary integrations.

explanation: We inspect every machine in the small environment and do not use the optional sampling permission.
Some procedures receive quarterly verification and validation, but staffing gaps leave others overdue.
customerRisk: Outdated instructions may delay recovery or lead to incorrect handling of agency information.
providerCompensation: Operators test restoration steps monthly and review known documentation gaps weekly.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can request current recovery instructions and keep independent copies of their content.

explanation: Servers receive weekly reviews, but some identity and process resources miss the Class B monthly drift-detection interval.
customerRisk: Unnoticed access or procedure changes may affect agency information.
providerCompensation: We restrict administrative access and review change tickets weekly.
agencyCompensation: Agencies should periodically review their accounts and report unexpected permissions.

explanation: Stable servers are reviewed quarterly, but some non-machine resources have not received complete detection checks within six months.
customerRisk: Hidden weaknesses in stable resources could undermine service recovery.
providerCompensation: Operators test the restoration path monthly and record discovered weaknesses.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can ask for the last review date for dependencies they rely on.

explanation: We prioritize availability exposures, but cannot yet demonstrate all Class B impact reductions within the applicable PAIN timeframes.
completionTargetExplanation: Supplier fixes and incomplete tracking prevent a reliable completion estimate.
customerRisk: Other exposures may persist beyond recommended intervals and affect agency content or access.
providerCompensation: We disable affected optional features and retain tested backups.
agencyCompensation: Agencies should avoid critical workloads and keep sensitive information outside this service.

explanation: Routine maintenance resolves outage-related findings, but other residual vulnerabilities lack consistent scheduling.
customerRisk: Deferred weaknesses may accumulate and affect agency information.
providerCompensation: Weekly reviews retain those findings and prioritize any change in likely impact.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can ask about unresolved findings before extending service use.

explanation: We patch exposed KEVs promptly, but do not yet consistently remediate fully mitigated KEVs by catalog due dates.
customerRisk: Failure of an interim mitigation could restore a known exploitation path.
providerCompensation: Operators recheck filtering and disable affected optional components.
agencyCompensation: Agencies should disconnect affected integrations until remediation is confirmed.

explanation: Operators perform vulnerability detection on every machine at least once every seven days, covering more than the Class B representative-sample minimum.
This is a Rev5 Class B offering, so the 20x-specific machine-verification rule does not apply; VDR-TFR-MVF is the relevant rule.
Weekly checks verify availability, but full validation of machine configurations against intended behavior remains incomplete.
customerRisk: Undetected configuration errors may affect agency access or information.
providerCompensation: Operators compare key service settings and test restores monthly.
agencyCompensation: Agencies should use this workspace only for noncritical public information.

explanation: Weekly reviews evaluate major exploitation prerequisites, but supporting evidence is incomplete for some findings.
customerRisk: We may underestimate vulnerabilities affecting agency workspaces.
providerCompensation: The operator treats uncertain findings conservatively and disables exposed optional features.
agencyCompensation: Agencies should keep sensitive data elsewhere and request review of concerning findings.

explanation: Reviews cover direct internet exposure, but indirect payload paths through imports and logs are not fully assessed.
customerRisk: A vulnerable internal component could process hostile input despite network isolation.
providerCompensation: We restrict imports and filter external input at the service boundary.
agencyCompensation: Agencies should avoid untrusted uploads and disable unused integrations.

explanation: Weekly reviews assign provisional PAIN ratings emphasizing outages, but confidentiality, integrity, and multi-agency effects need fuller analysis.
customerRisk: Incomplete impact estimates may understate the consequences for agency customers.
providerCompensation: We restrict the service to public-information use and escalate uncertain ratings.
agencyCompensation: Agencies should verify that their content is public and avoid mission-critical dependencies.

explanation: Our manual checklist assumes exploitation can be automated unless we retain technical evidence proving otherwise.
The small team tracks each finding separately and has not established contextual vulnerability groups.
completionTargetExplanation: The small inventory currently makes individual tracking more practical.
customerRisk: Related findings may receive inconsistent handling and consume review time.
providerCompensation: A single operator checks the full register each week for shared causes.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can request one explanation for related findings affecting their workspace.

explanation: Operators verify obvious scanner errors, but lack time to investigate every potential false positive.
customerRisk: Unconfirmed findings can divert effort from genuine agency risks.
providerCompensation: Uncertain findings remain open and high-impact cases receive priority.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can ask for the evidence behind any dismissed finding.

explanation: Reviews consider availability, reachability, and basic exploitability, but do not consistently document all eight contextual factors.
customerRisk: Incomplete context may hide privilege escalation or interacting vulnerabilities.
providerCompensation: We limit privileges and review known incidents during the weekly assessment.
agencyCompensation: Agencies should describe their use case and avoid sensitive or critical workloads.

explanation: Weekly updates cover major findings, but some verification and validation activity is missing from reports to necessary parties.
customerRisk: Agencies may lack a complete basis for continued-use decisions.
providerCompensation: We provide the underlying operations log on request through controlled sharing.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can request missing records and limit use until questions are resolved.

explanation: Our spreadsheet includes identifiers and current ratings but lacks complete historical reductions, evaluation times, and next-reduction details.
customerRisk: Agencies may not be able to judge whether risk is declining on time.
providerCompensation: Operators retain dated work notes and review unresolved findings weekly.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can request those notes and keep independent records of important exposures.

explanation: Accepted findings include reasons and identifiers, but evaluation times and agency mitigation details are incomplete.
customerRisk: Agencies may misunderstand the duration or consequences of accepted risk.
providerCompensation: We list known limitations in the monthly report and offer a manual review.
agencyCompensation: Agencies should seek clarification before accepting affected use cases.

explanation: The operator shares risk information with necessary parties through restricted channels and removes exploit-enabling technical detail from public notices.
Monthly summaries cover maintenance and outages, but do not yet summarize every detection and response activity.
customerRisk: Agencies may overestimate the breadth of our review program.
providerCompensation: The full operations log remains available through controlled sharing.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can request separate testing and disclosure records.

explanation: We do not currently exercise optional public vulnerability disclosure and continue required controlled reporting to necessary parties.
All necessary parties receive the same human-readable monthly report, with implementation gaps and service limitations identified.
The weekly register flags elapsed 192-day cases, but we do not yet consistently mark findings accepted when missing that limit is foreseeable.
customerRisk: Agencies may mistake a long-term exposure for work that will finish within the limit.
providerCompensation: The monthly report lists supplier delays and known unresolved limitations.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can ask whether any planned fix lacks a credible completion date.

explanation: The spreadsheet has no automated JSON retrieval interface, and a small team has not funded one.
completionTargetExplanation: Funding and implementation timing remain undecided.
customerRisk: Agency tools cannot automatically monitor historical activity.
providerCompensation: We provide manually assembled history through controlled sharing on request.
agencyCompensation: Agencies can reconcile the history with monthly reports and retain their own copies.

explanation: Every detected finding receives a weekly initial review, but complete evaluation under VER-EVA is not consistently finished within seven days.
customerRisk: Incomplete evaluations may delay agency decisions about exposures between reviews.
providerCompensation: The operator escalates suspected high-impact findings immediately and tracks unfinished assessments.
agencyCompensation: Agencies should request completed assessments before expanding use beyond noncritical public information.

explanation: We exercise the Class B option to treat internet-reachable likely exploitable findings above N3 as reportable incidents until reduced to N3 or below.
We also exercise the Class B option to treat non-internet-reachable likely exploitable N5 findings as reportable incidents until reduced to N4 or below.
